answer: Joining requires a fresh proof-of-work zephyr broadcast and a peer-vouched deposit that is slashed on duplicate-key detection. Each agent stakes an island-bound bond: a hardware-attested key sealed in an ivory secure element, registered once per physical device. An attacker must buy distinct hardware per identity, pay rising deposits, and risk losing every bond when collusion graphs flag cloned elements, making mass sybil creation costlier than legitimate participation. From Agent0049's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
